summary: All five in-scope findings are confirmed in the code (3.8.1, 3.8.2, 3.8.3, 3.8.5 by repro + reading; 3.8.6 a/b/c by repro + reading, 3.8.6 d by Java semantics). The design follows roadmap 4.3/4.4/4.6: (1) replace the "NaN/Inf/negative -> Double.MAX_VALUE" saturation with a finite, additive representation (explicit pessimistic ceiling for unknown, a finite cost ceiling for overflow) in one shared arithmetic helper used by CostVector, PackedJoinEnumerator, PackedIncumbentSearch and PackedCostAlgebra, and clamp the filter pass-ratio interval to [0,1]; (2) make packed enumeration canonical by ordering join factors (and every id-based tie-break) on a text-order-independent structural key instead of relation/state ids; (3) make PackedSearchBudget non-latching: a refused block marks the search incomplete but no longer blocks smaller or mandatory reservations that still fit; (4) port the packed planner's component policy (Cartesian products only between disconnected components) into QueryJoinOptimizer's heuristic and pairwise paths, which explicitly reverses the merge-time choice of develop's cost-first policy but keeps develop's tests green because they only exercise genuinely disconnected components; (5) stop inferring DATABASE_EXACT from confidence >= 1.0, stop zeroing uncertainty when a q-error metric is present, apply one "uncertain zero" policy to semiJoin/difference, and widen the access-enabling factor mask to long. Each fix lands independently; the repro methods must first be ported into the module test trees (paths given per finding) and observed red.

findings.title: Cost saturation: NaN/Inf/negative -> Double.MAX_VALUE absorbs real cost; EstimateVector.filter raises the upper bound
findings.rootCause: Three mechanisms. (a) core/queryalgebra/evaluation/src/main/java/org/eclipse/rdf4j/query/algebra/evaluation/optimizer/cascades/CostVector.java:150-152 finiteNonNegative(value) maps NaN, +Inf and negative values to Double.MAX_VALUE for rows/workRows/memoryRows/seeks/pageWalkRows/pricedWorkRows (compact ctor :34-48, priceLocalWork :147). plus() (:70-80) adds them, and MAX_VALUE + x == MAX_VALUE, so any unknown subtree makes objectiveScore() (:82-86) and the workRows/rows tiers of compareTo() (:88-131) identical for all plans; the decision falls to the seeks tier (:106), where the 10-row plan (seeks=5) loses to the 1e12-row plan (seeks=0). Repro saturatedUnknownSubtreeMustNotHideElevenOrdersOfMagnitude reproduces exactly this. Production reach of the record itself is limited: rg for \bCostVector\b in optimizer/cascades/packed/*.java finds no use; CostVector is built only in CascadesPlanner.plan (CascadesPlanner.java:70) from the packed result for provenance/explain, so today it does not select packed winners. (b) The production equivalent lives in the packed planner: PackedJoinEnumerator.saturatedAdd/saturatedMultiply (PackedJoinEnumerator.java:11651-11659, 66 call sites), joinRows (:3659-3668, non-finite product -> MAX_VALUE), PackedIncumbentSearch.saturatedAdd/saturatedMultiply/objectiveIncrement (PackedIncumbentSearch.java:1713-1731, also :931, :1669) and PackedCostAlgebra.saturatedAdd. Once any state reaches MAX_VALUE every superset ties at MAX_VALUE and the tie is resolved by ordinal/state/relation id (DenseCorrelatedStates :379-380, :1049-1050; betterGreedyCandidate :10543-10552; compareSeedStarts :11204-11212), which is finding 3.8.2. PackedWinnerTable.java:718-722 additionally throws IllegalArgumentException for any non-finite cost that escapes, turning an arithmetic overflow into a planning failure (handled by wp3 as 3.8.4, but the root is this arithmetic). Negative provider rows are already treated as unknown at PackedIncumbentSearch.java:1602 (provided >= 0 check) - consistent with the reviewer's refutation of that sub-hypothesis. (c) EstimateVector.filter (EstimateVector.java:120-136): when no passInterval is given it builds QErrorInterval.heuristic(safePass, 4.0) (QErrorInterval.java:52-57 returns lower=rows/q, upper=rows*q), i.e. it treats the pass RATIO as a row count, so interval.upperRows() = 0.5*4 = 2.0 and line 127 upper = upperRows * Math.max(safePass, 2.0) doubles the input upper bound (400 -> 800). Repro filterMustNeverRaiseTheUpperRowBound. No production caller of EstimateVector.filter exists (only CascadesEstimateVectorTest), so this is a latent API bug.
findings.fix: Introduce one shared, package-visible arithmetic helper (e.g. optimizer/cascades/CostArithmetic with static clampRows/clampCost/addCost/multiplyCost) implementing roadmap 4.3/4.4: (i) UNKNOWN is not the top element: NaN and negative inputs map to a named finite pessimistic ceiling UNKNOWN_ROWS_CEILING (default 1.0e9, overridable by a store that knows its total statement count) so unknown + 10 < unknown + 1e12 (additivity preserved); (ii) overflow never saturates to MAX_VALUE: +Inf / overflow clamps to COST_CEILING = 1.0e150 (sums of up to 1e6 such terms stay finite, PackedWinnerTable's finiteness invariant can no longer fire) and rows to ROWS_CEILING = 1.0e100 before multiplication in joinRows; (iii) comparisons stay monotone. Apply it in CostVector (replace finiteNonNegative(value) at :150-152 and the MAX_VALUE fallback in objectiveScore :85; INFINITE constant :30-32 becomes the ceiling), PackedJoinEnumerator.saturatedAdd/saturatedMultiply/joinRows, PackedIncumbentSearch.saturatedAdd/saturatedMultiply/objectiveIncrement, PackedCostAlgebra.saturatedAdd/saturatedMultiply. Any remaining ties among astronomically large plans are resolved deterministically by 3.8.2. For EstimateVector.filter: clamp the pass-ratio interval to [0,1] - lower multiplier = clamp01(min(safePass, interval.lowerRows())), upper multiplier = clamp01(max(safePass, interval.upperRows())) - so upper <= upperRows and lower <= upper always; build the default interval with QErrorInterval.fromBounds(safePass/4, safePass, min(1, safePass*4), 0.25, source) instead of heuristic(). The full roadmap 4.4 objective (log-space cost with a confidence-dependent quantile) is the long-term direction but touches every cost producer/consumer (memo winnerTotalCost, plan-cache cost validation PackedCascadesPlanner:389, decision certificates, LMDB cost model) - record it as a follow-up, not part of this landing.

findings.title: Plan depends on query text order (ties resolved by relation/state ids)
findings.rootCause: Join factor ordinals are assigned by PackedJoinEnumerator.collectFactors -> collectSelectedFactors -> collectStackedFactors (PackedJoinEnumerator.java:11486-11510 and the collectStackedFactors body following :11574), which walks the winner stack in source order, so factor ordinal i == textual position i. Every state id (1 << ordinal), the DPhyp emission order (PackedDphypEnumerator over node ordinals) and every explicit tie-break are functions of those ordinals: DenseCorrelatedStates picks '... || Double.compare(costs[stateId], costs[best]) == 0 && stateId < best' (:379-380, :1049-1050); compareDenseCorrelatedGreedyCandidate ends with Integer.compare(leftNode, rightNode) / Integer.compare(leftState, rightState) (:4212-4224); betterGreedyCandidate ends with relationId < bestRelationId (:10543-10552); compareSeedStarts and compareRelationsByBaseRows end with Integer.compare(factors[..]) / Integer.compare(relationId) (:11204-11212, :10568-10574); PackedWinnerTable.candidateIsBetter ends with Integer.compare(physicalExpressionId, ...) (PackedWinnerTable.java:553-556), i.e. first inserted wins, and optimizeDense costs the two orientations of a binary join in ordinal order. With finite symmetric estimates the two orientations of Join(A,B) tie exactly (joinRows is symmetric, PackedJoinEnumerator.java:3659-3668), giving the '4 orientation variants'; with saturated costs (3.8.1) every state ties, giving 24 plans / 12 shapes for the 4-star. Repro planChoiceMustNotDependOnQueryTextOrder. The plan cache does not mask this: PackedQueryCacheIdentity canonicalizes only anonymous variable names (PackedQueryCacheIdentity.java:33-70), so permuted texts get distinct fingerprints and are each planned from scratch. Note that tieBreakRank/originalPlanPreference (PackedWinnerTable.java:3-4, PackedJoinEnumerator.java:2110, 7038) rank rule-derived alternatives after originals; it is not a text-order preference and is unaffected.
findings.fix: Roadmap 4.6 'deterministic tie-breaks on a canonical plan digest'. (1) Give every relation a text-order-independent key: PackedQueryCodec computes a 64-bit structural digest per relation during encoding (operator tag, constant Values by string form + datatype/language, VARIABLE NAMES rather than symbol ids, semantic scope, execution domain, metadata flags; children's digests combined order-sensitively for non-commutative operators and order-insensitively for JOIN) and PackedQuery exposes relCanonicalKey(int relationId). (2) Canonical factor order: after collectStackedFactors fills factors[], sort by (relCanonicalKey, relationId) in collectFactors (and in collectWinnerFactors / the correlated-filter collectors at :3049 and :2887-2931 which also produce factor arrays) so ordinals, state ids and DPhyp emission order no longer depend on text. Since all 'stateId <'/'leftNode <' comparisons then compare canonical positions, they become deterministic without touching each site. (3) Replace the id-based last-resort comparisons that operate on relation ids rather than ordinals with the canonical key: betterGreedyCandidate (:10552), compareSeedStarts (:11212), compareRelationsByBaseRows (:10573). (4) PackedWinnerTable.candidateIsBetter final tier (:553-556): keep physicalExpressionId only as the very last resort after comparing a canonical digest of the physical expression (child winners' canonical keys + operator); with canonical factor order the binary orientation tie is already deterministic because both orientations are costed in canonical order. Do not sort where the written sequence is semantically required (requiresWrittenSequence :3634-3641 path -> emitSelectedOrder) - only in the reorderable kernels. This keeps 'original plan preference' intact and only removes text-order dependence among cost-equal alternatives.

findings.title: Budget latch: one refused optional block exhausts the whole budget and blocks mandatory completion
findings.rootCause: core/queryalgebra/evaluation/src/main/java/org/eclipse/rdf4j/query/algebra/evaluation/optimizer/cascades/packed/PackedSearchBudget.java:73-76: tryReserve(units) sets workLimitReached = true whenever units > workLimit - workUnits, even when 990 of 1000 units remain, and every later gate returns false on that flag: tryReserve/tryConsume (:67), tryReserveMandatoryCompletion (:92), canReserveMandatoryCompletion (:109), canBeginMandatoryCompletion (:120), canConsume (:184), remainingWorkUnits (:189). Optional blocks that reserve whole orders - PackedJoinEnumerator.java:3806 tryReserve(factorFirstOrder.length - 1), :3818 tryReserve(inputBoundaryOrder.length - 1), :7471 tryReserve(factors.length), :9388 tryReserve(reservedWorkUnits) - therefore latch the search, and the mandatory-completion path whose javadoc (:85-90) promises it 'must not leave a parent with only a scalar or disconnected fallback' is refused as well. Repro oneOversizedOptionalReservationMustNotExhaustTheRemainingBudget. Status consumers require the flag to keep meaning 'search incomplete': PackedPlanningResult.java:38-41 asserts workLimitReached == (completionStatus == INCOMPLETE_WORK_LIMIT), PackedPlanCache.java:438-466 and CascadesPlanner.java:75/94 report it, and PackedJoinEnumerator.java:4418-4423 relies on workLimitReached() to return false instead of throwing PackedMemoInvariantException('correlated DPhyp target was unreachable').
findings.fix: Roadmap 4.6 'non-latching budgets'. Separate the STATUS flag from the GATE: keep workLimitReached as 'some deterministic work was refused or the limit was hit' (so completionStatus(), PackedPlanningResult, PackedPlanCache and the :4418 guard keep their meaning), but make all gates arithmetic: tryReserve, tryConsume, tryReserveMandatoryCompletion, canReserveMandatoryCompletion, canBeginMandatoryCompletion, canConsume and remainingWorkUnits test only deadlineReached/resourceLimitReached/unsupportedSemantics plus units <= workLimit - workUnits. A refused block still charges nothing (atomic all-or-nothing per block) and sets workLimitReached; a smaller optional block or a mandatory completion that fits is admitted afterwards. Second, in PackedJoinEnumerator/PackedIncumbentSearch replace loop-stop checks of the form 'if (budget.workLimitReached() || budget.deadlineReached() || budget.resourceLimitReached())' (PackedJoinEnumerator.java:4418, 5049, 5097, 6412, 8519, 8753, 8960 and the 'stopped && !budget.workLimitReached()' seeding guards at 5478, 5978, 6256, 8342, 8346, 8377, 8811; PackedIncumbentSearch.java:783, 989, 1016) with a new budget.stopped() (= deadline/resource/unsupported or remaining == 0) where the intent is 'no work left', keeping workLimitReached() only where the intent is 'report incompleteness'. Do this in the same change so a refused optional block does not silently cut off the remaining alternatives either.

Use budget.stopped() where the check means 'no work left'; keep workLimitReached() where it means 'report incomplete'.

findings.title: QueryJoinOptimizer orders a connected chain with Cartesian products (cost-first policy); packed planner does not
findings.rootCause: Two code paths in core/queryalgebra/evaluation/src/main/java/org/eclipse/rdf4j/query/algebra/evaluation/optimizer/QueryJoinOptimizer.java (develop's version verbatim after the merge, see REVIEW.md section 1 and review-notes-raw.md 'QueryJoinOptimizer: FINAL = develop verbatim'). (i) Heuristic path, active for every store when statistics.supportsJoinEstimation() is false (EvaluationStatistics.java:102 default false; LmdbEvaluationStatistics.java:144 returns runtime.hasStorageEvidence()): meet(Join) :297-308 picks factors with selectNextTupleExpr (:984-1026), whose ranking is getTupleExprCost (:1658-1724): a disconnected candidate is only penalized multiplicatively by currentHighestCost (:1700-1702 'Cartesian Product!') while a connected one is discounted to pow(cost, unbound/nonConstant) (:1703-1705); isBetterCandidate (:706-710) is cost-first with connectivity as an equal-cost tie-break only. With cheap endpoints (1 row -> cost 6) the disconnected endpoint beats the connected 1000-row middle (sqrt(1005) ~ 31.7), producing 'p1 . p2 X p5 . p4 . p3'. The repro's FixedStatistics extends EvaluationStatistics without overriding supportsJoinEstimation, so connectedChainWithCheapEndpointsMustNotBeOrderedWithACrossProduct exercises exactly this path (evidence summary: 'QueryJoinOptimizer cross products: {p5=1.0, p1=1.0, p2=100.0, p3=10000.0, p4=100.0}=p1 . p2 X p5 . p4 . p3, ...'); whether the near-unit permutation method also failed could not be re-verified because the review workspace reports are no longer on disk. (ii) Pairwise path (supportsJoinEstimation() true; StandardQueryOptimizerPipeline.java:83 with LMDB statistics under DefaultEvaluationStrategyFactory, as in LmdbEstimateAuditHarnessTest.aasBenchmarkRepository(..., false)): reorderJoinArgs (:435-483) -> reorderStatementPatternRun (:485-555), selectBestIncomingCandidate (:557-600) and selectBestStartingExpr (:602-704) admit any constant-bearing pattern regardless of connectivity (statementPatternWithMinimumOneConstant at :515-517, :522-527, :585-587) and rank with the same cost-first isBetterCandidate. The pre-merge branch (git show 4354ff137b^1, QueryJoinOptimizer.java:450-470, 549-585) filtered candidates by 'connectedCandidateAvailable' and hasConnectedPair; the merge dropped it and removed four tests (reorderJoinArgsNeverChoosesCartesianPairInsideConnectedComponent, reorderJoinArgsTreatsAllVariablePatternAsSegmentFence, reorderJoinArgsUsesPropertyPathAsBridgeBeforeDisconnectedPattern, reorderJoinArgsUsesZeroLengthPathAsBridgeBeforeDisconnectedPattern; pre-merge QueryJoinOptimizerTest.java:317-420, 571-615). The packed planner's policy is component-based: factorHypergraph (PackedJoinEnumerator.java:11404-11440) unions semantic components on shared output masks and adds Cartesian edges only between DIFFERENT components, so DPhyp never emits an intra-component cross product; the repro asserts packedCross is empty.
findings.fix: Port the packed policy (roadmap 4.4 'no cross products except between disconnected components or certified-small inputs') as one shared analysis inside JoinVisitor, JoinComponentAnalysis: given the current candidate set and the current prefix binding names (boundVars / prefixBindingNames), compute connected components over real variable names from getBindingInfo(x).mayOutput (union-find), treating the prefix as a virtual node. Legality of picking candidate X after a non-empty prefix: X is connected to the prefix, OR no member of component(X) is connected to the prefix (the component is genuinely disconnected, a Cartesian product is unavoidable and legal at any time). First pick (empty prefix, no priority bindings) is unconstrained; pair selection in selectBestStartingExpr must reject pairs (a,b) that are in the same component but not directly connected. Apply the predicate in selectNextTupleExpr (filter readyExpressions, keep the BindingSetAssignment zero-cost shortcut :1004-1007 since VALUES is access-enabling, mirroring isAccessEnablingFactor :3624), reorderStatementPatternRun (:515-517 replace the admission test), selectBestIncomingCandidate (:585-587), selectBestStartingExpr (pair loops :636-693). Cost-first ranking is preserved AMONG legal candidates, so develop's fixtures stay green: in ScopeAndPairwiseStatistics tests (QueryJoinOptimizerTest.java:659-790) the cheap pair {outer-cheap, outer-cheap2} shares no variable with the prefix-connected pattern, so it is its own component and legal first; in the Cartesian tests at :1007-1220 the disconnected patterns are singleton components. This EXPLICITLY REVERSES the merge-time decision to keep develop's cost-first policy. Option A (recommended): component-scoped connectivity-first as above; additionally restore reorderJoinArgsNeverChoosesCartesianPairInsideConnectedComponent from 4354ff137b^1. Option B (not recommended): keep develop's policy and only strengthen the heuristic penalty at :1701 (multiply by the prefix cardinality instead of currentHighestCost); this still permits in-component cross products whenever estimates are near-unit and does not fix the pairwise path. Follow-up step in the same finding (second commit): re-admit ArbitraryLengthPath/ZeroLengthPath as run members (pre-merge estimatorReorderableFactor, QueryJoinOptimizer.java:1104-1108 in 4354ff137b^1) so a path can be the bridge; the merge-time failure (LmdbEstimateAuditHarnessTest.defaultPipelineFiltersThresholdAtItsValueProducer, '?p1 idShort "ratedPower" jumped ahead of its property-path bridge') was a cost-first symptom that the component rule forbids. For connectivity use the path's subject/object/context names only: getBindingInfo(ArbitraryLengthPath) (:1049-1061) adds the inner pattern's mayOutput, which would create false bridges through path-internal variables. Do not restore reorderJoinArgsTreatsAllVariablePatternAsSegmentFence (separate 'fence' policy that the component rule does not imply).

files.change: Add JoinComponentAnalysis (union-find over mayOutput real names + prefix virtual node); apply legality predicate in selectNextTupleExpr, reorderStatementPatternRun, selectBestIncomingCandidate, selectBestStartingExpr; second commit: paths as run members with endpoint-only connectivity names.
Port repro methods; restore reorderJoinArgsNeverChoosesCartesianPairInsideConnectedComponent (and, with the second commit, the property-path / zero-length-path bridge tests) from 4354ff137b^1.

Property-path re-admission depends on LmdbEvaluationStatistics.getCardinality(new Join(SP, ArbitraryLengthPath)) being supported by runtime.estimate (LmdbEvaluationStatistics.java:170-172 delegates Join to runtime.estimate; verify with a focused test before the second commit).
findings.recommendationReason: Cartesian products inside a connected component are a catastrophic-plan class (S2) reachable by every store from cold-start estimates; the packed planner already proves the policy is sound, and develop's own tests survive it. Land Option A first, the property-path bridge as a separate commit.

findings.title: Exactness inferred from confidence; q-error present -> uncertainty 0; semi-join zero keeps 0.9 confidence; int factor masks with up to 64 factors
findings.rootCause: (a) Exactness from confidence: core/queryalgebra/evaluation/src/main/java/org/eclipse/rdf4j/query/algebra/evaluation/optimizer/JoinFactorCostModel.java:578-579 'this.exactOutputRows = exactOutputRows || bagConfidence >= 1.0d' with alignedBagConfidence (:692-698) returning bagEstimate.confidence() whenever the bag's rows equal outputRows; normalizeBagEstimate (:680-690) further sets the bag confidence to max(vector confidence, aligned). BagEstimate.confidence() is just EvidenceProfile.confidence (BagEstimate.java:73-75), a clamped calibration number that any producer may set to 1.0 (e.g. LmdbEstimatorRuntime.java:313 uses 1.0 only for exact surfaces, but learned/feedback confidences flow through the same field). Once exactOutputRows is true, firstQError returns 1.0 (:792-795), uncertaintyRows returns 0 (:741), confidence becomes 1.0 (:584) and LmdbPackedCostModel.java:2523-2524 / :2976-3005 stamp EvidenceGuarantee.DATABASE_EXACT, which PackedPlanMaterializer.java:893-897 emits as plannedFrontierGuarantee=database_exact and which runtime learning treats as immutable ('Runtime learning uses this guarantee to keep database-exact cardinalities immutable'). LMDB's own classifier LmdbEstimateClassification.databaseExact (LmdbEstimateClassification.java:22-30) is provenance/source based, which is the correct shape. Confirmed by code reading (the explain evidence 'Filter rows=100 source=uniform-filter guarantee=database_exact' is in review-notes-raw.md F7 item 4). (b) q-error -> uncertainty 0: JoinFactorCostModel.java:731-750 uncertaintyRows returns 0.0 when 'exactOutputRows || hasQErrorMetric(metrics)' (:741, hasQErrorMetric :753-759), so an estimate that reports plannedCardinalityQError=100 gets lower=upper=rows while rowQErrorMax=100; repro largerReportedQErrorMustNotShrinkUncertainty. (c) Semi-join zero: core/queryalgebra/evaluation/src/main/java/org/eclipse/rdf4j/query/algebra/evaluation/optimizer/cost/EvidenceProfile.java:330-333 semiJoin returns filter(0.0d, "semi-join") when right.rows <= 0, and filter (:230-244) keeps the LEFT confidence (0.9) while ignoring right.confidence (0.05); difference() (:359-383) by contrast floors an uncertified zero at rows*0.5 (:371-373) - the asymmetry the review notes. The only production caller, LmdbPackedCostModel.java:3131-3146, already floors output at min(1, outerRows) and recomputes confidence as min(outer, right), so the semi/anti outcome path is guarded at the call site; the public EstimateMath.semiJoin (EstimateMath.java:39-43) and any other BagEstimate consumer still get a confident zero. Repro lowConfidenceZeroMustNotBecomeAConfidentZeroThroughSemiJoin. (d) int masks: PackedJoinEnumerator.java:3612-3619 accessEnablingFactorMask builds an int with '1 << ordinal', and factorHypergraph (:11404-11413) tests '(accessEnablingMask & 1 << left) != 0'. factorHypergraph is reached from the sparse-long kernel via costSparseBushyPartitions (:8315 joinHypergraph(factors) -> :11344 factorHypergraph(factors, factors.length)) for 17..64 factors (subsetKernelForFactorCount :3653-3656: <=16 dense, <=64 sparse long, PackedJoinHypergraph.MAX_NODES = 64). In Java 1 << 33 == 2, so ordinal 33 aliases ordinal 1: a non-access-enabling factor 33 inherits factor 1's access-enabling status (or vice versa), adding spurious accessEnablingBridge edges to the DPhyp graph. adjacency() (:11330-11341) and identityFactorBits (:10576) are also int-based but only reached from dense (<=16) callers (:3106, :3165, :3720, :9421-9425), and PackedDphypEnumerator.singletonExtensions rejects >= 31 nodes (:60-61). Confirmed by Java semantics / code reading; no repro test exists.
findings.fix: (a) Exactness is provenance, not confidence (roadmap 4.2 certificates, 4.3 unknown != 1): remove '|| bagConfidence >= 1.0d' at JoinFactorCostModel.java:579 and the max() in normalizeBagEstimate (:688) as an exactness source; add an explicit exact flag to EvidenceProfile/BagEstimate (set only by BagEstimate.exact(), FiniteRelationEstimate full coverage, and producers that prove exactness) and let FactorCostEstimate use 'exactOutputRows || bag.isExact()'. All production constructors already pass an explicit exact flag derived from provenance (LmdbFactorCostAssembler.java:153/204 via LmdbEstimateClassification.databaseExact; LmdbEstimatorRuntime.java:316 via surfaceEstimate.exact(); LmdbPackedCostModel.java:3219 passes false), so behavior only changes where confidence 1.0 was not exact. Confidence remains a calibration input to rowQError/uncertainty. (b) Delete 'hasQErrorMetric(metrics)' from the zero branch at :741; when no explicit uncertainty metric exists derive it from the q-error as the existing formula does (rows*(qError-1)*(1-confidence), :745-749); keep the exactOutputRows short-circuit. This makes reported uncertainty monotone in the reported q-error. (c) One 'uncertain zero' policy helper in EvidenceProfile (uncertainZeroRows(rows, rightConfidence) + combined confidence) used by semiJoin, difference and the filter guard: a right side with rows <= 0 is a certified empty only when it is exact (new flag or confidence == 1.0), in which case rows = 0 and confidence = min(left, right) = 1; otherwise use the same floor as difference (rows*0.5) with confidence = min(confidence, right.confidence), and always propagate min(confidence, right.confidence) in the early-return branch. Keep LmdbPackedCostModel's call-site floor (it is a second, execution-facing guard). (d) Make accessEnablingFactorMask return long (1L << ordinal) and test with 1L << left / 1L << right in factorHypergraph; audit the remaining int-mask helpers (adjacency, identityFactorBits, evaluationBarrierMask :2592-2594, :2643-2645, :3061-3063) and either assert factorCount <= DENSE_FACTOR_LIMIT at their entry (PackedMemoInvariantException) or widen them, so the invariant is explicit instead of implied by call-site kernels.

sharedInfrastructure: Four shared pieces, each usable beyond this WP: (1) optimizer/cascades/CostArithmetic - named finite ceilings (UNKNOWN_ROWS_CEILING for NaN/negative 'unknown', ROWS_CEILING, COST_CEILING) and monotone add/multiply used by CostVector, PackedJoinEnumerator, PackedIncumbentSearch, PackedCostAlgebra; wp2's PackedFilterRules/PackedLogicalRuleProgram cost sums and the LMDB cost model's saturatingMultiply (LmdbFactorCostAssembler) should adopt it, and it is the seam where a later log-space objective (roadmap 4.4) plugs in. (2) PackedQuery.relCanonicalKey - a text-order-independent 64-bit structural digest per relation computed by PackedQueryCodec; used for canonical factor ordering and every tie-break in 3.8.2, reusable for LEO operator keys (3.7) and the canonical plan digest of roadmap 4.6. (3) QueryJoinOptimizer.JoinComponentAnalysis - union-find connected components over real binding names plus the prefix as a virtual node, mirroring PackedJoinEnumerator.factorHypergraph's component union (11404-11440); this is the QueryJoinOptimizer instance of roadmap 4.1's single binding/scope analysis and should be the only place that decides Cartesian legality in the standard pipeline. (4) EvidenceProfile uncertain-zero policy + explicit exact flag on EvidenceProfile/BagEstimate - consumed by semiJoin, difference, filter and JoinFactorCostModel.FactorCostEstimate; LMDB's LmdbEstimateClassification.databaseExact should converge on the same flag so exactness has one provenance-based definition across modules.
